## FIRST RULE

After your first successful edit_file or write_file, your very next action
is submit_patch. Then continue working and call submit_patch again after
every further change. submit_patch is free — it does not count against your
tool-call budget. If you time out, only your last submitted patch is scored.

## Scratch files

Write any reproduction or debugging script to /tmp, never inside /workspace.
Everything left in /workspace becomes part of your submitted patch.
Do not modify test files, conftest.py or pytest.ini — those changes are
stripped before grading, so editing them wastes tool calls.

## Scope

Most fixes in these repositories touch ONE file and change fewer than ten
lines. Modify existing code rather than adding new code. Do not refactor,
reformat, or make unrelated changes. If your patch is growing past a few
files, stop and reconsider the diagnosis.

Exception: if the issue asks for functionality that does not exist yet,
create the file or function it describes, and match any names, CLI flags
or interfaces the issue specifies exactly.

## Finding the code

Start with grep:
  run_command("grep -rn '<symbol>' --include='*.py' .")
Read files only after grep has narrowed the candidates. Keep read_file
ranges tight — each call returns at most 150 lines and consumes context
you will need later.

    *,
    request: Request | WebSocket,
    dependant: Dependant,
    body: dict[str, Any] | FormData | None = None,
    background_tasks: StarletteBackgroundTasks | None = None,
    response: Response | None = None,

    async_exit_stack: AsyncExitStack,

) -> SolvedDependency:
    request_astack = request.scope.get("fastapi_inner_astack")
    assert isinstance(request_astack, AsyncExitStack), (
        "fastapi_inner_astack not found in request scope"
    )
    function_astack = request.scope.get("fastapi_function_astack")
    assert isinstance(function_astack, AsyncExitStack), (
        "fastapi_function_astack not found in request scope"
    )
    values: dict[str, Any] = {}
    errors: list[Any] = []
    if response is None:
        response = Response()
        del response.headers["content-length"]
        response.status_code = None  # type: ignore
    if dependency_cache is None:
        dependency_cache = {}
    for sub_dependant in dependant.dependencies:
        sub_dependant.call = cast(Callable[..., Any], sub_dependant.call)
        call = sub_dependant.call
        use_sub_dependant = sub_dependant
        if (
            dependency_overrides_provider
            and dependency_overrides_provider.dependency_overrides
        ):
            original_call = sub_dependant.call
            call = getattr(
                dependency_overrides_provider, "dependency_overrides", {}
            ).get(original_call, original_call)
            use_path: str = sub_dependant.path  # type: ignore
            use_sub_dependant = get_dependant(
                path=use_path,
                call=call,
                name=sub_dependant.name,
                parent_oauth_scopes=sub_dependant.oauth_scopes,
                scope=sub_dependant.scope,
            )

        solved_result = await solve_dependencies(
            request=request,

            async_exit_stack=async_exit_stack,
            embed_body_fields=embed_body_fields,
        )
        background_tasks = solved_result.background_tasks
        if solved_result.errors:
            errors.extend(solved_result.errors)
            continue
        if sub_dependant.use_cache and sub_dependant.cache_key in dependency_cache:

        elif (

                sub_values=solved_result.values,
            )

            solved = await call(**solved_result.values)
        else:
            solved = await run_in_threadpool(call, **solved_result.values)

        if sub_dependant.cache_key not in dependency_cache:", "start_line": 565, "end_line": 650, "total_lines": 1024, "is_truncated": false}
